candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record describes diffuse, generalized T2/FLAIR white matter hyperintensity involving all cerebral lobes without mention of hydrocephalus or ventriculomegaly, alongside a progressive rigid-akinetic syndrome, cognitive decline, psychosis, and mildly elevated CSF protein with no pleocytosis — a constellation consistent with gliomatosis cerebri. NPH would require ventriculomegaly as its hallmark and does not explain diffuse lobar white matter infiltration; the candidate diagnosis is a different diagnostic entity entirely.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus (NPH) is a distinct entity characterized by ventriculomegaly with normal CSF opening pressure, classically presenting with the triad of gait disturbance, dementia, and urinary incontinence; it does not account for the diffuse supratentorial white matter T2/FLAIR hyperintensity across all cerebral lobes without ventriculomegaly, nor the psychotic episodes, rigid-akinetic syndrome, and CSF findings described here. Gliomatosis cerebri is a diffusely infiltrating glial neoplasm producing extensive white matter signal abnormality, which fits the imaging and clinical profile far better.

case_quality_flags: Diagnosis of gliomatosis cerebri ideally requires histopathological confirmation or advanced MRI/spectroscopy; the record relies on imaging and CSF alone, which may limit certainty.
Absence of biopsy data noted; differential includes leukodystrophy, CNS vasculitis, or other infiltrative processes, but gliomatosis cerebri remains most consistent with the described findings.
